record.paper_title: Exploring Progressions: A Collection of Problems
record.original_question: Partition the even positive integers into blocks {2}, {4, 6}, {8, 10, 12}, …, so that the nth block consists of n consecutive even integers and begins at n(n − 1) + 2. Determine the sum of the numbers in the nth block.

evidence.quote: We divide the even natural numbers into groups as follows: {2}, {4, 6}, {8, 10, 12}, . . . ; the nth group contains n even numbers starting with (n(n − 1) + 2). Find the ’sum of the members of the nth group.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Partition the even positive integers into consecutive blocks $B_1, B_2, B_3, \dots$ such that, for each positive integer $n$, the block $B_n$ consists of exactly $n$ consecutive even integers whose smallest element is $n(n-1)+2$. Thus $B_1 = \{2\}$, $B_2 = \{4,6\}$, $B_3 = \{8,10,12\}$, and in general $B_n = \{n(n-1)+2,\; n(n-1)+4,\; \dots,\; n(n-1)+2n\}$. Determine, as a closed-form expression in $n$, the sum of all members of the block $B_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a standard elementary exercise. The block $B_n$ is an arithmetic progression of $n$ terms with first term $n(n-1)+2$ and common difference $2$, so the sum equals $n\bigl(n(n-1)+2\bigr) + 2\cdot\frac{n(n-1)}{2} = n^3 + n$. The closed form is well known and the problem is fully solved.

status_evidence.title: Arithmetic progression sum formula
status_evidence.snippet: The sum of an arithmetic progression with n terms, first term a and common difference d is n(2a+(n-1)d)/2.
status_evidence.claim: Applying the standard AP sum formula yields n^3+n directly, confirming the problem is a routine solved exercise.
